newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine may extend voucher privatisation deadline.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine may extend voucher privatisation deadline.

text.p: Ukraine's parliament will probably extend its mass privatisation programme to the end of 1997, the State Property Fund chairman said at the weekend.
"The majority of deputies are saying that they are in favour of extending the deadline to the end of next year," Yuri Yekhanurov told reporters.
Currently each of Ukraine's 52 million people -- adults and children -- has until mid-1997 to invest a certificate nominally worth about $275 to buy shares in a privatised company.
So far only 45 percent have started buying shares with the certificates.

About 80 percent of Ukrainians have picked up their certificates and the government, hoping to include all citizens in the privatisation process, has extended the pick-up deadline to January 1, 1997, from October 1 this year.
The Fund, the state privatisation agency, hopes to sell 70 percent of shares in 3,000 medium- and large-sized enterprises in 1997, Yekhanurov said. --Yuri Kulikov, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
